title: National Government to support Commission of Inquiry into UBS Loan
description: Deputy Prime Minister and Attorney General Davis Steven says the national government is committed to supporting the Commission of Inquiry into the K3 billion UBS loan deal.   The Inquiry is set to commence on 27th January 2020 and end on 27th July 2020, when the report will be presented to the Prime Minister.    However, during the public hearing on Monday, this week, it was announced the commission needs an additional K27 million to fund the inquiry.

asr.full_text: the public hearing by the full Commission on Monday highlighted the six phases the Commission will cover in the six month period to complete the inquiry the full Commission includes sir Salam O India and John Gilmore as chairman of the Commission and Commissioner respectively the Commission will also consist of Councils and solicitors however because of the delays within the office of the solicitor-general and the board of the National procurement Commission there was no solicitor or counsel present we are still able to deal with preparatory work for the Commission to be able to sit in early 2020 to conduct the actual inquiry in terms of receiving evidence. The inquiry into the three billion kina UBS loan, Kamsafcay report produced by the ombudsman commission concluded that the leaders and persons mentioned in the findings had failed to comply with the proper procedures relating to laws on the borrowing of the Australian dollar loan . The report named James Maropé and Peter O'Neill as Denn and minister and Prime Minister respectively to face the leadership tribunal. We took this undertaking to call our commission of inquiry knowing full well the challenges that we face. But the Merapi-Steevion government is aware that our people have placed the corruption, ...the corruption perception and the fight against that perception is a priority... ...unfortunately or fortunately its going to cost us money but... ...I call that a need full expense. And of course as you know the public accounts committee is currently conducting it's duty... ...they too have their needs in terms of resourcing. The police department continues to do its work. And we are going to manage these issues because our people demand it and it's our duty and responsibility as government to deliver it. The COI needs an additional funding of 27 million kina which was approved by the Prime Minister in September. This is to cover all aspects conclusively in relation to the borrowing of the 3 billion kina loan. The fact in this country is a very clearly to restricts known registered Papua New Guinea lawyers from holding themselves out of performing functions and duties of a lawyered without being properly certified and that processed that is clear and that I'm aware that the Commissioner has requested and that process is currently underway for proper licensing of non-Papua New Guinan resident lawyers or registered lawyers. So I'm happy that we do not conduct a commission of inquiry that is flawed, that is not in setup and operate according to law. Sekle Gunga, NTV News.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it concerns news coverage of a government commission investigating a three-billion-kina UBS loan and reporting on the inquiry's timetable and findings. The additional 27 million kina refers to commission resourcing approved by the Prime Minister, not a viewer-directed payment, investment opportunity, or request for private information. The hearing imagery and official setting are consistent with this public-inquiry context, although the sampled frames do not establish every detail of the proceedings.
